\CRchapter{39}{The Sentence Finished}{Days 160–162 · Tallow 11–13, Y.H. 813}{Low Kiln and the Weir, Sill}
\CRepigraph{A hand held back from the iron is still a hand that knows where the iron stands. The kiln takes four pulls and leaves the fifth where nobody looks; the river counts water over water and enters nothing. A sentence allowed to finish is a sentence nobody can be made to give back.}{A saying of the Clay Yard, spoken at the second working of Tallow}

\begin{CRchronicle}{39}
After the first Account-day the firing month went back to its work. The boy was one hundred and sixty days old on the first morning and one hundred and sixty-two on the last, and nobody said so. The kiln breathed in fours with a gap; the fire missed its fifth with its payer unnamed, and the river kept its note. Sella Vail gave her instruction to wool, fire, pot and broom, never to the basket, kept her half-pace and left the widow’s mark where it hung: a morning, a shelf and a dusk are not openings. The yard went around the clean dark line, the thaw, the broken birth-slates and the place where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out. At the shelf she sent a wet-pot neighbour’s cost to the pot, then reached a finger beneath the front edge where the charcoal lay, without looking, and brought it away unread.

On the second morning three or four men went low into the back room and got no name. Jorra Vail came through with slate dust ground small as meal on both forearms, told a pot it would do, and withheld its note from a kiln-master. Then, for the first time under that roof, his bent finger went to the cold damper and stopped. Sella had begun \emph{The fire’s low. It wants---}; the hand waited while she finished \emph{It wants feeding}, then moved the tongue a hair’s breadth. No one spoke. The boy filed the fraction on a place of its own --- a change held and not spoken, not a reconciliation, not a hearing. Tarn’s stroke went on over the flagstones without the half-check; nine stoppings stood and the loan stayed uncalled.

On the last day the finished reeds had become a direction counted in the carrying arm, which keeps the weight and not the cost. Downriver at the Weir the reed-cutter tied one knot with his teeth and hid his cord; Orra Weir gave the ninth of Ilmen where a figure was asked, and Mira Silt answered a thin run with \emph{Ask the river}, her second twist twice beneath the creel. A child’s foot stayed dark in three turns of wool; the reading of the cold bought nothing at two paces. The soft-cuffed clerk stayed set for a measure nobody called.

At the going of the light she carried him home, going wide around the pan’s gone place, the trough and the rack space. She set him on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, told the fire it was the thaw and \emph{The house will keep it}, and set the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand. In the small hours his file was exact and worthless: six hearings with no seventh, nine stoppings with no payer. One hundred and sixty-two stood exact, complete and unspent. The fire missed its fifth; the charcoal waited for a hand that was not his and a day that has not come.
\end{CRchronicle}
